verdicts.note: S3 has both quoted lines ('fair share', 'too much wealth in too few hands'); S16 blames expiry of ACA credits on billionaire tax breaks; clerk roll 190 shows her No on H.R. 1. Three independent sources, so +2 high stands.
Roll 33 confirms her Nay on the HALT Fentanyl Act (passed 312-108; Strickland voted Yea). The gun-reform priority is weak evidence on this axis, but the vote supports +1 at medium.
LCV Action Fund is on the campaign home page (S2) and in the pamphlet (S1); roll 114 confirms her Nay on H.J.Res. 88.

Re-fetched S6 (Defending Democracy): it confirms she has refused corporate PAC money since her first race. Beyond that it covers voting access only, with no term-limit, dark-money or RCV plank, so +1 medium is right.

Re-fetched S4: her federal plan is pole_a (protect and strengthen the ACA, Medicaid flexibility, lower medication costs). But she cites sponsoring the bill that created Washington's Universal Healthcare Commission, and S16 has her 'sick care system' remark, which leans toward universal coverage. Her federal platform does not mention Medicare for All, so the evidence does not support -1 or +1. 0 at medium is a fair reading of evidence that points both ways.

+1 is right; +2 would overstate it. Clerk records confirm Aye on the Massie amendment (roll 243; 104-314), Nay on the S. 1071 NDAA (roll 320), and Yea on both the Iran (roll 85) and Lebanon (roll 201) War Powers resolutions. S13 frames her vote as 'no more additional funding for offensive weapons' while she keeps humanitarian aid. That is pole_b on Israel aid and on war powers. Against that, S14 says her House NDAA No was over LGBTQ+ floor amendments, not Pentagon spending, and in the same bill she secured added Defense Community Infrastructure Program funding. Her dossier has no audit-or-cut-the-Pentagon position. The votes are record evidence, so high confidence is justified.

S2 bundle text: 'Income Tax? Climate Commitment Act? Washingtonians are being burdened by big government. It's time to say enough!' and 'Keep money in family pockets'. S3 quotes her on 'high taxes'. Medium is appropriate because she has no specific tax proposal.
Naming the CCA as a burden is a pole_a marker, and her 'science-based stewardship' line keeps her short of -2. -1 medium is a conservative call.

Her only reform plank is the U.S. Term Limits pledge and 'Congress should be a service, not a career' (S2). It is explicit and repeated, and it is squarely pole_b. But it is one plank: she states nothing on PAC money, dark money, RCV or direct democracy. Randall's single plank (refusing corporate PAC money) is scored +1 medium in the same contest. Scoring one pole_b plank at +2 here overstates her position and makes the two inconsistent.

S2 offers telehealth expansion, incentives for rural doctors and keeping rural clinics open. Her site says this 'bypasses partisan debates'. The axis runs from protecting ACA/Medicaid within existing structures to universal public coverage. She says nothing about the ACA, Medicaid, drug prices or coverage models. The placement rests on an inference that her proposals are 'within the existing system', not on a stated position, so the direction holds only at low confidence.

Her S2 Title IX section has two explicit statements: biological males in girls' sports 'erases the progress of the last 50 years', and the locker-room privacy objection. Sex-based sports eligibility is the first pole_a marker. She has no abortion position, which keeps confidence at medium.

Her pamphlet pledges 'building our Naval dominance' (S1). S2 has a Naval Readiness plank and 'ships that can fight today'. Her 'not DC consultants / not bureaucratic overhead' lines argue about where defense money goes, not how much, so they are not pole_b. -1 medium fits pro-readiness evidence that covers only the Navy and district jobs.
